description: The shim behavioral contract (design §6.1, frozen interface §14 item 2), exercised for real by supervisor/src/shim.test.ts + shim.integration.test.ts (Task A4); this kit encodes the same scenarios as fixtures so describeAttemptSupervisorContract can assert them generically once A5 assembles the full supervisor.

scenarios.name: outcome-file-atomicity-kill-9-between-temp-and-rename
scenarios.description: A kill -9 lands after the temp outcome file is fsynced but before the atomic rename to meta/outcome.json.

scenarios.name: fingerprint-vs-pid-reuse
scenarios.description: A fingerprint binds (pid, start-time); a recycled PID with a different start-time must read as not-alive.

scenarios.name: outcome-nonce-mismatch-rejected
scenarios.description: readOutcome rejects an outcome file whose nonce does not match the attempt's nonce.

scenarios.name: group-kill-zombie-pinning
scenarios.description: Group-kill ordering does not reap the harness leader until AFTER the group signal, so the PGID cannot be recycled under the kill.

scenarios.name: subreaper-adoption
scenarios.description: A daemonizing grandchild that detaches from the harness re-parents to the shim (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER on Linux), not to init — so it is still visible to the group scan.

scenarios.name: signal-survival-raced-ahead-success
scenarios.description: The shim traps SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP and ignores them at the shim's own level; it relays cancellation to the harness subtree only. A natural exit 0 that races ahead of a SIGTERM aimed at the subtree is recorded as such.

scenarios.name: env-tag-present-from-fork
scenarios.description: JINN_ATTEMPT_* is present in the shim's own environment from the instant the shim process exists (set by the supervisor at spawn, inherited across fork) — closing the invisible-orphan gap between fork and exec.
